If, whatever face thou paintest
In those eyes, grows pale with pleasure,
15 If the fainting soul is faintest
When it hears thy harp’s wild measure,
Wonder not that when thou speakest,
Of the weak my heart is weakest.

paragraphs.source_en:
As dew beneath the wind of morning,
20 As the sea while Whirlwinds waken,
As the birds at thunder’s warning,
As aught mute, yet deeply shaken,
As one who feels an unseen Spirit
Is my heart when thine is near it.

paragraphs.source_en:
26 To —— (‘I fear thy kisses,
gentle maiden’)
Published in 1824 without date; included in 1839 among the Poems Written in 1820. No fair
copy has been traced, and there is no transcription in either Mary Copybk 1 or Mary Copybk
2. S.’s untitled draft in Nbk 11 115–16, a mixture of roughly pencilled lines and some fair copy
in ink, is both longer and less uniformly achieved than the two stanzas printed by Mary in
1824 and which are given below. Although the draft is untidy, those two stanzas are clearly
worked out in the form in which they appear in 1824, so the simplest hypothesis would be
that Mary extracted them directly from Nbk 11. It is always possible that S. himself prepared a
fair copy which supplied her text, but there is no necessity to suppose its existence. The order
in which S. composed the three stanzas that comprise the draft on the facing pages 115–16 is
